extracted.intended_audience: SEC officials, institutional investors, corporate governance lawyers, and investor stewardship stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A policy comment letter arguing the SEC should preserve its historical no-action oversight role under Exchange Act Rule 14a-8 and not permit unilateral issuer exclusion of shareholder proposals absent staff review. The page explains why the Division’s announced change harms shareholder voice, increases litigation/reputational risk, and should be reversed promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareholder proposals are an essential, cost-effective tool
rubrics_metrics.description: “Shareowner proposals, which are almost always nonbinding, are an essential and cost-effective tool for expressing the collective voice of a company’s shareowners on particular matters, and have made important contributions to corporate governance over the last 50 years.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: promoting annual director elections and establishing simple majority vote requirements; efficient way for institutional investors to promote governance without costly board replacement campaigns. Remove barriers that would limit this tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC Division of Corporation Finance should remain a fair arbiter
rubrics_metrics.description: CII has long publicly supported the view that the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (SEC Staff) is a fair arbiter for implementing the shareholder rule, and that CII members take comfort from Staff oversight of shareholder proposal exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff review through the no‑action process provides an independent opinion on a corporation’s claimed basis to exclude proposals; this oversight benefits both shareholders and corporations by resolving disputes impartially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to Staff’s role should follow public comment / due process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement was issued “without the benefit of public comment,” resulting in a fundamental change in how the SEC Staff approaches Rule 14a-8 for the current proxy season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public consultation is necessary for changes that may negatively affect shareholder rights, to preserve due process and market confidence; notice-and-comment should precede substantive departures from historical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff should not accept a company’s representation of a “reasonable basis” to exclude without review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement indicates the SEC Staff will accept a company’s representation that it has a “reasonable basis” to exclude a proposal and won’t object to that conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deference to an issuer’s self-assessment risks permitting lawful-but-questionable exclusions and diminishing shareholders’ ability to have proposals considered; Staff should continue to evaluate legal bases for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accessibility of Rule 14a-8 for shareholders meeting existing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement could potentially limit the ability of shareowners to file shareholder proposals that would otherwise meet the existing requirements of Rule 14a-8 and improve corporate governance and long‑term shareholder value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the existing Rule 14a-8 eligibility and filing framework so proponents who meet the rule can submit proposals and have them considered by shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid increasing board-level instability, reputational and legal risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than alleviating pressure on corporate boards, the Statement could result in greater board-level instability through unnecessarily increasing issuers’ reputational or legal risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards that unilaterally omit shareholder proposals may face vote-no campaigns, litigation, heightened scrutiny, and reputational headlines — regulators and issuers should weigh these consequences before broad withdrawal of Staff oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Staff involvement to reduce costs, confusion, complexity and delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical record: commentators opposed discontinuing Staff involvement because it caused problems of costs, confusion, complexity and delay; no change to the Staff’s role was effected in 1983 for these reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing Staff engagement in no-action requests helps resolve disputes efficiently and lowers transaction costs for proponents and issuers; removing that role likely increases dispute costs and uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect minority and smaller proponents from disproportionate burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing or significantly narrowing the Staff’s role risks eroding investor voice and imposing disproportionate burdens on minority and smaller proponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design should avoid forcing smaller/less-resourced proponents into more costly or complex processes (litigation, activism) to vindicate their rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companies must have a defensible, documented basis for exclusions if Staff withdraws
rubrics_metrics.description: CorpFin’s new policy places more responsibility (and litigation risk) on companies and their counsel to assess whether they have a defensible basis for excluding proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Staff declines to opine, issuers should ensure board rationale and documentation for exclusion decisions are robust to mitigate litigation and fiduciary‑duty exposure; absence of Staff review shifts disputes to courts or activist campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary policy changes affecting shareholder rights should be reconsidered and reversed expeditiously
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement “applies to the current proxy season (October 1, 2025 – September 30, 2026) …” and CII believes the new process should be reconsidered and reversed as soon as practicable, but no later than the end of this proxy season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short‑term suspensions of oversight that affect shareholder rights should be rescinded promptly to avoid long-term harm to governance and market confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound corporate governance requires shareholders can submit and vote on important governance proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: “Sound corporate governance is critical to long-term returns … CII members have a strong interest in seeing that shareholders can submit and vote on shareholder proposals that raise important corporate governance issues.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should enable shareholder voice on material governance matters because good governance protects long-term shareholder value; regulators should preserve mechanisms that allow consideration of such proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource/timing considerations should not justify substantive departures from established policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC cited “current resource and timing considerations following the lengthy government shutdown and the large volume of registration statements and other filings requiring prompt staff attention” as the reason for the Statement, but CII is concerned this rationale effects a fundamental change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational constraints (e.g., temporary resource shortages) should not be used to make substantive, precedent‑setting changes to processes affecting shareholder rights without careful review and stakeholder input.
